unsupported: Frustrated by the lack of hands-on guidance for marine electronics, he launched the business to teach fellow anglers how to use their sonar and GPS units effectively.
The company remains independently owned and operated.

The shop functions as a full-service marine electronics retailer: it sells fish-finding and navigation units, handles professional installation on customers’ boats, and provides one-on-one training sessions tailored to each angler’s needs.

The owner emphasizes a personal, undivided-attention approach rather than group classes, helping clients interpret sonar returns, adjust settings, and integrate electronics into their fishing strategy.
The customer base consists of recreational and tournament anglers, boat owners, and anyone upgrading or switching brands of marine electronics.

Central Kentucky Sonar serves the broader recreational fishing industry across central Kentucky, with clients ranging from weekend hobbyists to competitive bass fishermen seeking to maximize their on-water efficiency.
That gap drives the company’s differentiator: personalized, on-the-water-style instruction that turns complex electronics into practical fishing tools.
